column4: For every n>2 and g>0, existence of n-solvable K with topological g4(K)>g. Requires exact solvable-filtration conventions and higher-order signatures; no bounded full-scope construction audited. AIM parked.

For every integral homology sphere and knot, existence of a topological homology concordance to S3. Universal surjectivity is not reduced to any finite certificate; smooth/topological distinctions essential. AIM parked.

For every K,J, all prime-power branched-cover rational homology cobordisms imply concordance. The concordance category and compatibility of cobordisms are unstated; choosing smooth versus topological changes target. No small witness established.

For every K,J, integer homology cobordism of every rational surgery is assumed, conclusion concordance. Category, orientations and peripheral compatibility matter. Matching finitely many slopes cannot certify antecedent.

Existence of a uniform bound on commutator length for all volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of S3. Component/regularity and volume conventions need primary definitions; perfectness alone gives no uniform bound.
Literal NIH funding list contains no mathematical proposition or quantified unknown. Routing it as an open problem cannot create discovery scope.
Every fusion category C and simple X: FPdim(C)/FPdim(X) algebraic integer. Requires coefficient-field/category hypotheses; integral or solvable subfamilies do not answer the universal assertion.
Existence of a conceptual construction of the even half of 4442. Object and meaning of conceptual are external; classification-level construction has no bounded certificate route here.
Consistency that lim^p A=0 simultaneously for all p. Diagram A, index set, and degree range absent; p=0 literal shortcut would be a wording change, not discovery.

Prove inconsistency of the displayed universal Sigma1 forcing principle with aleph1,aleph2 parameters and preserving both. Ambient language and permitted extra parameters must be fixed before diagonal arguments.

Which analogues of PFA at aleph2 imply |X|<=2^aleph1 for every Hausdorff X without an aleph2 discrete subspace? Analogue not specified; known cardinal inequalities under stronger axioms cannot settle it.

Relative consistency of tree property at aleph_(omega+1) together with reflection of all stationary subsets there. Reflection domains/cofinalities need source conventions; forcing construction is far beyond small certificate screening.

Classify E and countable G for strict E<E^[G], including effective variants. Reducibility and measurable/effective coding not specified. Trivial G yields equality but is merely one parameter instance.

For every n and polynomial p in minors, characterize nonnegativity on all TN matrices. Expanding determinants gives a universal real-closed-field formula with all minors>=0; quantifier elimination decides rational/algebraic input coefficients. Arbitrary real coefficients require an effective representation; this classical route is not credited.

All finite simple S and finite G with order-dividing bijection G->S: must G be simple? Bijection forces equal cardinality; matching order distributions via Hall constraints is a diagnostic, not an all-simple-groups proof.

Every finite group should have a presentation whose removal of any relator makes the presented group infinite. Minimal irredundance proves only nonredundancy, not infinitude; no full-scope construction.

Every finite-group power graph that has no induced P4 should be chordal. An induced cycle of length>=5 contains P4, while a C4 of cyclic-subgroup containments yields a P4 by taking a prime-power subgroup of one upper cyclic group outside the other. Short hand derivation retained in bounded-checks; primary and prior routes parked, no discovery proposal.

Every nontrivial finite G and choice of Sylows Hi: one conjugator x simultaneously minimizes every Hi intersection Hi^x by inclusion. Individual minimality or coprime product heuristics do not imply simultaneous feasibility.

Every finite simple transitive permutation group should have derangement proportion>=89/325. Faithful nontrivial action and simple-group conventions need primary scope; trivial-degree or cyclic endpoint corrections earn no credit.

Every finite primitive action with a regular suborbit: all alpha,beta admit gamma with both pair stabilizers trivial. Common neighbor in Saxl graph is the full target; a positive-valency bound alone is insufficient.

For every finite 3-group T, a nontrivial characteristic C must work for every finite overgroup G with Sylow T, equating intersections with derived groups. T=1 is a literal endpoint defect, not a substantive counterexample; no transfer theorem under full intended scope.

Existence of one infinite G such that for every subset A all maximal direct-product complements B have equal cardinality. Arbitrary subsets prevent reducing the assertion to finite subgroup tilings; no construction.

For every nilpotent automorphism group A of finite soluble G, ask a bound on Fitting height in |A| and |C_G(A)|. Main question readable, but literal trailing Isaacs fragment is damaged. Coprime/cyclic special-case results cannot silently supply missing hypotheses.

Every finite semi-abelian group as explicitly recursively defined should be monomial. Induction must handle quotients and semidirect products at the character-induction level; solvability alone does not imply monomiality.

Every group should satisfy the stated finite-F epsilon permutation approximation. Hamming metric d is unstated. Residual finiteness and amenability give only families; finite search cannot refute soficity.

Existence of a finite nonabelian odd-order G with exactly |G|/17 conjugacy classes. Extraspecial p-groups have commuting probability (p^2m+p-1)/p^(2m+1), so isolated family computations would be insufficient; no exact witness obtained.

For every integer n>39, p(n) should not divide n!. Executed exact partition dynamic programming and divisibility for n=40..500; zero counterexamples. Finite negative results supply no full-scope route; stop, no larger sweep.

Every Cartesian product of Raikov complete minimal Hausdorff topological groups should remain minimal. Infinite product uniformities and minimality must be controlled; finite products or complete factors separately are not enough.

Countable G admitting a countable dense partition should admit pairwise disjoint finite Fn meeting each open U eventually. Empty open set makes the literal definition impossible; intended nonempty-open convention must be checked, and endpoint repair earns no credit.

Defines codegrees and sigma(G), then asks whether constant k can be 4, without stating the inequality containing k. No proposition is supplied; do not reconstruct it from the title or guessed character-theory bounds.

Uniform bound on derived length for all finite weakly ab-maximal groups, defined by all subgroup abelianization indices. Need exclude nonsoluble groups or prove solvability as part of target; bounded order checks cannot answer it.

Separate existence questions for finitely generated simple and hereditarily just-infinite groups with exponential but nonuniform exponential growth. Existing nonuniform-growth constructions require exact simplicity/hereditary hypotheses; no short route.

One G with finite-index Gn and maps Gn->Z whose kernels are F_n but not F_(n+1), for every n. Fixed finiteness-level examples do not produce one group realizing all levels; construction/formal burden high.

For every RAAG and every element of its commutator subgroup, scl is rational. Free-group algorithms are only a special case; commuting graph relations alter surface optimization. No full rational polyhedron established.

For each distinct fixed primes p,q every finite group should embed in a finite group invariably generated by elements of exact orders p,q. Ordinary 2-generation or order-dividing constructions do not ensure universal conjugate generation.

Every hyperbolic G with finitely presented H meeting a positive power of every g: finite index? Primary Q1.10 explicitly gives the quasiconvex case only. Finite presentation does not by itself give quasiconvexity; no extension proof.

Every proper CAT(0) M with cocompact isometry group should have one R working for every pair a,b and a ray from a near b. Primary Q2.18 cites Ontaneda only with discrete cocompact action and nonzero compactly supported cohomology; those added assumptions cannot replace full scope.

For finitely presented H=F/N containing C^n for all n and finite nontrivial C, ask divergence of d_(F*F)(Nn) for doubles over C^n. Need presentation/rank d definition and embeddings; primary neighboring passage inspected, no uniform lower-bound mechanism.

Existence of a 3-complex not homotopy equivalent to any 2-complex but with H^3 zero for all local coefficients. Primary Q10.2 discusses domination by a 2-complex; obstruction theory, not ordinary integral H^3, is necessary.

For every finite graph, planarity or planar double cover or no finite planar cover. Primary Q13.3 itself notes a reduction without a reference. Arbitrary finite graph covers and double-cover reduction require a substantial global argument.

For every epsilon>0 there should be K(epsilon) bounding approximation size for every finite graph. Primary Q14 does not specify approximation metric locally; dense cut distance and bounded-degree local metrics give different quantitative tasks. No metric silently selected.

All locally convergent Gn and all fixed nonnegative integer k: chromatic root moments converge. Abért-Hubai v3 Theorem1.1 proves this under an absolute degree bound; selected proof and Theorem3.4 read. Without that convention, alternating empty graphs and K_m plus m^2 isolates gives first-moment limits 0 and 1/2, but this wording/domain issue earns no credit.

For each fixed d>=3, random d-regular independence ratio converges in probability along admissible n. Bayati-Gamarnik-Tetali v3 Theorem3 gives precisely the random regular optimization limit; independent-set definition and passage from configuration to simple graphs inspected. Selected proof invokes Theorem7 and Appendix B Proposition5, not independently replayed; full dependency audit not claimed.

Random d-regular graphs should converge locally-globally to weak closure of iid processes. Primary Q19 and nearby Q20 distinguish iid-action approximability. Local weak convergence alone does not prove local-global convergence or equality of coloring profiles.

For every degree k>1, a constant C(k)<1 bounds eventual return probability for all transient k-regular Cayley graphs. Primary Q33 and Q32 inspected; transience separately gives <1, not a uniform gap across all groups.

Every ergodic essentially faithful amenable action has groupoid cost1, plus every infinite ergodic action for finitely presented groups. Primary Q45 explicitly distinguishes essential faithfulness and infinitude. Cost of the orbit relation alone does not account for isotropy; do not import free-action theorem.

All generic linear forms, all positive d, claimed Hilbert function equals an omitted equation, with listed exceptional pairs and possible r=n+2,n+3. Missing S, characteristic, dimension convention and eq:RALF prevent literal verification; no statement replacement.

Qualitative request to clarify fracture models based on functional (2.31) against classical fracture and nonlinear elastostatics. Functional and intended comparison not present; no exact yes/no full-scope theorem in this record.

Literal omits eq:triv and Omega_k. Verified cached arXiv1503.05295v1 primary SectionII defines constant-coefficient homogeneous ODE of order k with distinct real parts of distinct characteristic roots. Source says open already k=3; this is a uniform zero bound over all equations/solutions, not per-equation finiteness. Retain original missing display flag.

Every real polynomial pair p,q: characterize restrictions on roots of p+iq from root locations of p,q. Cached primary Problem4 is broad and cites Fisk; Hermite-Biehler/interlacing cases are classical and do not yield full classification. No countable finite certificate target specified.
